title: Treasury International Capital (TIC) monthly release (December 2026 data) — the first February vintage this calendar tracks, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, re-fetched direct by THIS event's own research session 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,181 bytes). The 2027 table's February row reads '18' in the Monthly column with the two Quarterly columns EMPTY and '26 - prelim.' standing in the SEPARATE annual-survey column — a single-cut monthly release published EIGHT DAYS BEFORE the preliminary annual survey, not alongside it. Page header: 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. Reference month December 2026 by the page's own 1.5-month lag rule. PROMOTED from estimate 2026-09-09 on the bar the five TIC siblings and mts-october-2026-11-12 set — one named Treasury primary plus independent mechanical corroboration — with the no-self-confirm limit cleared because this is the event's own session re-fetching, not the tic-monthly-2027-01-19 sweep that discovered it. Corroboration, recomputed from scratch: with 5 U.S.C. 6103 holidays excluded (Presidents' Day 2027-02-15) the 11th business day of February 2027 is 2027-02-16, putting 02-18 at offset +2 business days, inside the page's published '11th business day plus 0 to 3 days' rule. STATED HONESTLY AND AGAINST THE SIBLING'S CASE: unlike 2027-01-19, this date does NOT discriminate the holiday-aware convention from the holiday-blind one — a holiday-blind reading lands on 02-15 at offset +3, also in-window, so the rule corroborates the published date here without testing anything. Across all 24 published 2026-27 dates the holiday-aware convention lands in-window 22 times and hits 9 exactly, independently reproducing tic-monthly-2027-01-19's count. TSY: is extended from auction schedule to release schedule on the precedent mts-august-2026-09-11, mts-october-2026-11-12 and tic-monthly-2026-09-16/10-16/11-18/12-15/2027-01-19 already recorded. CONFIRMED COVERS THE SCHEDULED DATE AND NOTHING ELSE: the same page carries the standing notice 'When Federal Government offices in Washington D.C. are closed on a release date, that date will be revised after offices reopen'. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-09) after reading the one proposal that created it, `from-tic-monthly-2027-01-19`, now shadowed. THE PROPOSAL'S PREMISE IS AMENDED, WHICH IS THIS ENTRY'S MAIN OUTPUT. It filed 2027-02-18 as the ORDINARY CONTROL for FT-tic-monthly-2027-01-19-3's revision test. It is not one: this is a FEBRUARY vintage, and February/March is precisely the bucket that ledger EXCLUDED post-hoc to make its result work (left in, its test is a flat null at p=0.78). A February vintage cannot be the clean control for a test whose result depends on Februaries being a different mechanism — that begs the question. What this date actually is, is the DISCRIMINATING observation for the exclusion itself, and the first February vintage this calendar has ever tracked. THE STATED GROUNDS FOR THAT EXCLUSION DO NOT SURVIVE A PRIMARY READ. The sibling attributed the Feb/Mar excess to the preliminary annual survey's benchmark feed; Treasury's own note (d) on this page says that convention is PRE-SEPTEMBER-2011 — 'Before September 2011, revised data back to the previous June was usually released in March to include preliminary data from the annual survey... The May release usually included the final results' — and that since December 2011 the monthly data are revised per note (c), i.e. on the Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct editions. Sequencing corroborates: this February monthly release publishes 2027-02-18, EIGHT DAYS BEFORE the 2027-02-26 preliminary survey, so the survey cannot be inside it. And the sibling's own Feb/Mar bucket is one February and two Marches, with its own text disqualifying the February one (2024-02, $745.9bn) as sitting across footnote 9's documented series break — leaving n=2 Marches. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds (16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is six weeks stale, no house playbook is macro-keyed). THE SCORED SESSION IS CONTAMINATED AND THE CONTAMINATION IS MEASURED: 2027-02-19 is monthly options expiration, where 2027-01-19's scored session carried only a VIX expiration. Measured rather than assumed, and it resolves benign — monthly opex sessions move the 10-year by 3.51bp against 4.02bp for non-opex sessions (t=-1.83, p=0.067, n=140 vs 2,850), and 14 of 111 verifiable TIC next-sessions since 2014-09-16 have already landed on one.
